Package bases

Class Natural

  • java.lang.Object
    • bases.Natural
  • public class Natural
extends java.lang.Object
    Represents an immutable, non-negative integer value along with a base in which to print its digits, which we can think of as a pair (base, value). For example, (2, 5) represents the integer 5 (in decimal), but it will show its digits as 101 (in binary) when printed.

    We require that the base is at least 2 and at most 36 for simplicity.

      • Natural

        public Natural​(int base,
               int[] digits)
        Creates an integer with the given digits in the given base. The digits should be provided with the smaller valued positions at the front of the array. For example, 321 base 10 would be passed in as [1, 2, 3].
        Parameters:
        base - the base used to represent numbers with digits
        digits - the non-null list of digits in the given base
        Requires:
        2 <= base <= 36 and digits.length >= 1 and all digits are between 0 and base - 1

      • plus

        public Natural plus​(Natural other)
        Produces the sum of this and other.
        Parameters:
        other - the natural number we are adding to this
        Returns:
        (this.base, this.value + other.value)
        Requires:
        other.base == this.base

      • leftShift

        public Natural leftShift​(int m)
        Produces a number whose digits, in this base, are the result of taking the digits of this number and shifting them to the left m positions, writing zeros in the now empty positions.
        Parameters:
        m - the number of positions we want the digits to shift left
        Returns:
        (this.base, this.value * this.base^m)

      • times

        public Natural times​(int val)
        Produces the product of this and (base, val).
        Parameters:
        val - the integer value we want to multiply this by.
        Returns:
        (this.base, this.value * val)
        Requires:
        0 <= val < this.base

      • times

        public Natural times​(Natural other)
        Produces the product of this and other.
        Parameters:
        other - the natural number we want to multiply this by
        Returns:
        (this.base, this.value * other.value)
        Requires:
        other.base == this.base
